chunks: "There is no wudu (ablution) required due to taenia worms and small worms; rather, they are like lice."
And this is when there is no excrement in it; but if there is excrement in it, then istinja' (cleansing of the private parts) and wudu (ablution) are required.

key_terms.الِاسْتِنْجَاءُ: cleansing of the private parts after excretion
key_terms.الْقَرْعِ: taenia worms or gourd-seed-like worms referred to in the ruling
key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: considered in the status of or treated as
key_terms.وُضُوءٌ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing for prayer

ai.seo_question: Does the emergence of small worms nullify wudu (ablution) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity and what nullifies wudu (ablution). It states that the emergence of small worms does not require wudu (ablution) by itself, as they are treated like lice, unless accompanied by fecal matter, in which case istinja' and wudu (ablution) become necessary.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.138 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
"There is no ablution required in the instance of taenia worms (or ticks and small worms), they are regarded like lice, and this applies if they do not have any waste matter,
However, if there is waste matter, then istinja (cleansing of the private parts) and ablution are required.”
